chunks: From Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) who said: Indeed, Allah the Exalted did not grant Satan authority over those who believe and do righteous deeds.
Except for what they voluntarily surrender of themselves.

key_terms.اسْتَحَلَّهُمْ: They made permissible for themselves / voluntarily surrendered

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for Satan having authority over believers?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq records Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifying that Satan's dominion is not inherent but contingent upon human choice, specifically when believers voluntarily yield to his whispers. This distinction underscores the Shia theological emphasis on *ikhtiyar* (free will), affirming that spiritual subjugation is a result of conscious surrender rather than divine predestination. Consequently, maintaining vigilance (*muraqabah*) allows the righteous to retain their autonomy against the devil's influence.
